column3: Repeats the focus verdict almost verbatim: people lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.
Mary and her son as a sign offer no clear route to worship-choice, loss, or final disclosure.
The secure station of the God-conscious supplies a distant positive contrast to the focus's manifest loss.
It directly joins loss of the self to unbelief and the certain gathering on the Day of Resurrection.
Receiving and confirming truth identifies the opposite response to the denial and loss named in the focus.
Fabricating a lie about God illuminates one route into the false worship condemned by the focus.
Conditional worship that reverses under trial is explicitly called loss in this world and the next.
Following guides who seek no payment supplies a limited contrast to self-serving worship.
Personal responsibility and the common return to God clarify how loss of the self is answerable at the end.
It explicitly names those who lost themselves and whose fabrications vanish from them.
Lying about God and rejecting truth lead to Hell, supplying the immediate moral route to the focus's loss.
The book's clarity does not materially develop the focus's worship, loss, or resurrection claim.
Those excessive against themselves remain God's servants and are called from despair, qualifying self-loss with a route of return.
Mocking the promised event is a limited contrast to the focus's certainty about the Day of Resurrection.
The command to protect selves and families from the Fire directly counters the focus's paired loss of self and family.
Light scales culminate in loss of the self and abiding in Hell, concretizing the focus's final loss.
Entry into abiding Hell gives the punitive outcome that follows the focus's manifest loss.
The plotters become the greatest losers, but the narrative does not develop the focus's worship or final-account setting.
Bearing one's own burdens and others' burdens on the Day of Resurrection explains the irreversible cost of misguidance.
Spouses and children form a created gift, supplying only background for the focus's loss of family.
Their inability to rise after punishment is not a sound route to the focus's final self-and-family loss.
“Do what you will” is paired with the contrast between being cast into Fire and arriving secure on the Day of Resurrection.
The promised elevated dwellings for the God-conscious provide a limited positive contrast to final loss.
Human willing remains under God's will, framing the focus's imperative without turning it into independent authorization.
Those without protectors besides God are gathered blind, deaf, and mute into Hell on the Day of Resurrection.
The sudden event prevents return to families, sharpening the focus's claim that family ties can be lost at the final crisis.
Cain's killing of his brother ends with his becoming one of the losers, an early instance of self-incurred loss.
It directly exposes worship of protectors besides God as a false mediation claim, the choice the focus leaves to its consequence.
The procession of the God-conscious into Paradise supplies the communal opposite of the focus's ruined family outcome.
It gives the universal diagnosis that humanity is in loss, which the focus specifies as final loss of self and family.
Those invoked besides God cannot remove or redirect harm, exposing the impotence of alternative worship.
Human possession of cattle does not add a clear route to the focus's account of worship or final loss.
God's acceptance of repentance supplies a distant alternative to a fixed identity as loser.
Turning away would have made the community losers without divine grace and mercy, a limited parallel to avoidable loss.
Revelation's clarification and light do not directly develop the focus's loss or worship-choice claim.
The Hour separates people, explaining how a single final event discloses divergent prior outcomes.
Worship besides God is reduced to unauthorized names, while worship of God alone is commanded.
God's sole dominion and creative authority make turning away to other objects of worship a fundamental misdirection.
Evil plotting closes back upon its own people, illustrating self-incurred loss rather than an arbitrary external penalty.
Manifest success for believers is a limited counterpoint to the focus's manifest loss.
The instruction to ask people of knowledge does not materially develop the focus's themes.
Defrauding others produces loss, but it is only an indirect ethical parallel to the focus's comprehensive loss.
Associators invoke God's will to excuse worship besides Him, directly engaging the focus's warning-like imperative.
Mountains and pathways for guidance offer no clear route to the focus's worship and final-loss claim.
Guidance versus misguidance identifies the losers as the outcome of being led astray.
Denying God's signs is explicitly presented as the act by which one becomes among the losers.
The queen's worldly sovereignty and throne do not add a clear route to the focus.
The command to rise and warn is not evidence for the focus's eschatological loss claim.
Those who deny Shu'ayb are the losers after their settled prosperity is erased, a narrative instance of reversed advantage.
God fulfills His promise by saving whom He wills and destroying the excessive, a broad outcome contrast only.
The self-reproaching soul gives a limited link to the accountable self that can be lost.
When fulfillment arrives, the people seek an impossible return and are explicitly said to have lost themselves.
The angels welcome the protected on the promised Day, supplying the positive final outcome opposed to manifest loss.
The desire to be upright identifies the positive human willing that contrasts with choosing worship besides God.
Noah treats forgiveness and mercy as what prevent his becoming among the losers.
The distinction between guided descendants and many defiantly disobedient offers only a broad response contrast.
God's willing formation of the person gives a distant grounding for the self, not a direct account of its loss.
The clear Book does not materially develop the focus's worship or eschatological loss.
Multiplied reward for faithful giving provides a limited positive contrast to loss.
Obeying a community against God would add only loss, making loss the consequence of misplaced allegiance.
God's complete knowledge is followed by disclosure of deeds on the Day of Resurrection, supporting the focus's final unveiling.
The question to the Samaritan has no clear route to the focus's claim.
A false assumption about God directly ruins its holders and makes them among the losers.
The final testimony over the People of the Book gives a limited link to resurrection disclosure.
Adam and his spouse face expulsion through an enemy's deception, a distant pair-based contrast to familial loss.
The statement about remembrance under God's will does not establish the focus's loss of self and family.
Preparing for yourselves while knowing that you will meet God gives only a limited personal-account link.
God's exclusive dominion, life-giving, and death-dealing authority undercuts rival worship and frames final accountability.
Clear proof separating disbelievers from their settled state supplies only a broad contrast of response to revelation.
Each party bears a nontransferable responsibility, clarifying the personal accountability involved in self-loss.
God alone grants favor, a limited corrective to claims that group membership grants control over divine goods.
No advocate can take responsibility for another before God on the Day of Resurrection, sharpening the focus's personal loss.
It calls all parties to worship God alone and refuse taking others as lords besides Him.
Guidance and good news for believers are too general to add a distinct route.
Asking people of knowledge does not materially develop the focus's worship or final-loss claim.
Forgiveness after obedient entry supplies a distant alternative to loss through disobedience.
The wrongdoers' lack of success offers a broad final-outcome contrast without a direct route to the focus.
Associating partners nullifies deeds and explicitly makes the person one of the losers.
The command to seek forgiveness within a community gives a distant alternative to incurable loss.
God's power to destroy all created beings exposes the incapacity of a deified creature and affirms exclusive dominion.
The false expectation that believers would never return to their families ends in a ruined people, lightly echoing family loss.
The arrival of a bearer of good news and warning after a gap supplies only a general alternative to ignorance.
Directing one's family toward prayer and patient worship positively answers the focus's concern for family loss.
Adam and his spouse confess wrong against themselves and name forgiveness and mercy as necessary to avoid being losers.
On the Day of Resurrection, alleged partners become the occasion of shame, directly exposing false association.
The earth's paths, rain, and varied plants do not add a clear route to the focus.
Feeling secure from God's plan is identified with being among the losers, a limited warning against false security.
Those who fabricate against God must face their assumption about the Day of Resurrection, when their claim is exposed.
The covenant not to worship Satan directly identifies a rival object of worship and its manifest enmity.
Communities subject to the realized word are called losers, connecting loss to a settled historical and final outcome.
The nullification of deeds in this world and the next gives a direct mechanism for comprehensive loss.
It names the greatest losers in respect of deeds, sharpening how apparent effort can end in total loss.
The believers' light and lasting gardens provide a positive final contrast to the focus's loss.
Faith occurs by God's permission while refusal to use reason brings defilement, a limited account of culpable failure.
God's creation and command establish sole sovereignty, indirectly grounding the rejection of worship besides Him.
Every self tastes death and returns to God, providing the universal passage in which final loss becomes visible.
Pilgrimage procedures do not materially develop the focus's worship-choice or final-loss claim.
God's responsibility for clarification does not add a distinct route to the focus.
The person denies the Hour yet assumes privileged treatment on return to God; the focus supplies the opposing verdict.
The explicit warning role supplies a limited rhetorical counterpart to the focus's public warning about loss.
The speaker fears the punishment of a tremendous Day if he disobeys God, setting the immediate judgment frame for the focus.
It immediately precedes the focus with the declaration of sincere worship directed to God alone.
Canopies of Fire above and below make concrete the final consequence of the focus's manifest loss.
Those who avoid worshipping false powers and turn to God receive the direct positive alternative.
The one against whom the word of punishment is due cannot be rescued from the Fire.
The paired command to act anticipates the focus's warning-like permission and its divergent consequences.
The question rejects being commanded to worship anything other than God.
It explicitly commands worship of God and gratitude, answering the focus's alternative worship.
Every soul is paid in full for what it did, making the final verdict disclosure rather than arbitrary loss.
The disbelievers' procession to Hell supplies the collective final outcome preceding 39:72.
Those who break God's covenant and sever what He ordered joined are explicitly the losers.
Turning back from faith makes deeds void in this world and the next, ending in the Fire.
Seeking a religion other than submission to God is rejected and makes one a loser in the next life.
Wealth and children cannot avail disbelievers against God, limiting the security of family and possessions.
Every soul tastes death and the full recompense is given on the Day of Resurrection.
Associating partners with God is singled out as the unforgivable wrong unless He wills otherwise.
It reiterates the gravity of associating partners and calls it far straying.
Evil done is repaid and no protector or helper can be found besides God.
Associating partners with God bars Paradise and fixes the Fire as the wrongdoer's abode.
On the Day of gathering, alleged partners are demanded and prove absent.
Those who deny meeting God are explicitly lost when the Hour arrives suddenly.
Those who take religion as play and are deceived by worldly life have lost themselves through what they earned.
Association would nullify even the prophets' deeds, directly linking false worship to loss of all work.
People come to God alone, leaving behind all they were given and all their claimed intercessors.
Jinn and humans are confronted with the warning they received before the Fire becomes their abode.
Those whose scales are light are the ones who have lost themselves.
Those who invent lies about God or deny His signs receive their appointed lot before final taking.
Denying God's signs and the meeting of the next life renders deeds void.
Hostile spending ends in regret and defeat, illustrating resources turned into loss.
God separates wicked from good and gathers the wicked into Hell.
Association with God renders works vain and fixes abiding in the Fire.
Worldly wealth and children can become the means of punishment rather than security.
Earlier peoples' deeds became worthless in this world and the next, and they were the losers.
Wealth and children are not to be admired when they function as worldly punishment and end in unbelief.
On the Day of gathering, God separates worshippers from their alleged partners.
Every soul is tested by what it sent ahead and returned to its true Master.
At the gathering, those who denied meeting God recognize that they had lost.
Every wrongdoing soul would ransom itself at the sight of punishment, but judgment is rendered justly.
It forbids calling on anything besides God that can neither benefit nor harm.
Those who seek only worldly life receive it there but have no share in the next life, where their works vanish.
The destroyed peoples wronged themselves; their gods besides God did not increase them except in ruin.
Most believers combine belief in God with association, directly identifying compromised worship.
Calls on others besides God are answered by nothing, exposing the futility of rival devotion.
The deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord are like ashes scattered by wind.
Satan disowns authority over his followers, leaving them no escape from the shared final outcome.
Setting up equals to God misleads from His path and leads toward the Fire.
Every community was sent the command to worship God and avoid false powers.
Associators see their alleged partners and openly acknowledge their false association.
Whoever wills the immediate world receives a limited share before facing blame and rejection in Hell.
Making another god alongside God ends in blame and abandonment.
When distress comes at sea, all those invoked besides God vanish from attention.
Taking God's servants as protectors besides Him is presented as a false choice leading to Hell.
The greatest losers are those whose worldly efforts are lost while they suppose they are doing good.
Denying God's signs and meeting makes deeds worthless and leaves no weight on the Day of Resurrection.
Hell is the recompense for disbelief and for treating God's signs and messengers in mockery.
Later people abandon prayer and follow desire, with a threat of destructive consequence.
God identifies Himself as the only God and commands worship directed to Him alone.
Turning from God's remembrance brings a constricted life and blind resurrection.
Every messenger receives the same declaration: there is no god but God, so worship Him.
Calling on what can neither harm nor benefit besides God is named far error.
Calling on a supposed protector that harms more than benefits is explicitly called manifest loss.
Association with God is portrayed as catastrophic fall with no stabilizing support.
When the trumpet is blown, family relations and mutual inquiry cease, directly qualifying reliance on kinship.
Taking one's own desire as a god identifies another form of rival worship.
They worship besides God what neither benefits nor harms and thereby support disbelief.
Associating another god with God is named among the grave acts that incur punishment.
Parents are not obeyed when they press association with God, even while they retain due companionship.
Those who take protectors besides God rely on a frail likeness, exposing misplaced dependence.
Believers are commanded to worship God alone wherever they must dwell.
The alleged partners have no intercessors, and their worshippers disavow them.
Luqman's counsel calls association with God a tremendous wrong.
Even parental pressure does not justify association; allegiance follows what turns to God.
Forgetting the meeting of this Day receives a reciprocal final consequence.
Those called besides God possess not even an atom's weight and have no share in divine authority.
Worldly life and the deceiver must not make people forget God's true promise.
On the final Day, the guilty are commanded to separate from the faithful.
Satan has led many astray, exposing the consequence of breaking the covenant against worshipping him.
Abraham challenges worship of things people carve, a concrete rejection of fabricated objects of devotion.
Those who disbelieved confess that their hatred of themselves is now evident in the Fire.
Those who deny the Book and the message will know the result when they are dragged in chains.
Chains and boiling water visualize the final cost of rejecting revelation.
The condemned are burned in the Fire after being driven through boiling water.
They are asked where their partners besides God are when final judgment arrives.
The alleged partners are declared lost, and the prior disbelief is exposed as the cause.
The alleged partners vanish from people, who realize there is no refuge.
Unauthorized religious legislation competes with what God permitted and incurs the decisive word of judgment.
Turning from remembrance assigns a devil as companion, showing the relational consequence of refusal.
Jesus declares God to be his Lord and theirs and commands worship of Him alone.
Those invoked besides God have no power of intercession except truthful witnesses.
Taking desire as a god leads to sealing of hearing and heart and a covering over sight.
None is further astray than one who calls besides God upon what cannot answer until the Day of Resurrection.
Disbelief makes deeds fail and brings ruin upon those who reject God's message.
Hating what God sent down makes deeds worthless.
Those who hold an evil assumption about God face the turning of evil upon themselves.
Disbelieving in God and His messenger ends in the prepared blazing Fire.
It explicitly forbids setting another god alongside God.
The named female deities introduce a direct example of the rival worship contested by the focus.
The alleged gods are only names without authority, followed by conjecture rather than guidance.
The hypocrites learn that self-deception, wishful waiting, and worldly illusion separated them from the believers.
Satan's party forgets God's remembrance and is explicitly identified as the losing party.
Satan's invitation to disbelief ends in mutual disavowal and the Fire.
Relatives and children will not benefit anyone on the Day of Resurrection, when God separates people.
Wealth and children are a trial, limiting their value as security against final loss.
The wives of Noah and Lot show that family relation cannot save one from the Fire.
Those who disbelieve in their Lord face the punishment of Hell and its wretched destination.
Receiving the record in the left hand reveals the personal final collapse of the condemned.
On that Day, no close friend asks about a close friend, directly limiting relational rescue.
The people of the right ask the guilty what drove them into Hell.
The fleeing question on the Day of Resurrection marks the collapse of all earthly refuge.
One who transgresses and prefers worldly life receives the Fire as final shelter.
Every soul will know what it has brought, a concise formulation of final disclosure.
No soul can avail another soul anything on that Day; command belongs wholly to God.
Receiving the record from behind one's back opens the sequence of final ruin.
Success belongs to the one who purifies the self, the positive counterpart to losing it.
Disbelievers among the People of the Book and associators are assigned the Fire as their abiding final outcome.
Even an atom's weight of good is seen, reinforcing the focus's disclosure of what was already done.
Heavy scales define the successful outcome, by contrast with the focus's comprehensive loss.
